_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Kyrgyzstan covering Scythian/Saka burials, Turkic khaganates, Karakhanid Islamisation, Mongol conquest, Kyrgyz ethnogenesis, Kokand Khanate dominance, Russian conquest 1876, Basmachi resistance, Soviet Kirghizia (cotton, literacy), 1990 Osh riots, independence 1991, Tulip Revolution 2005, April Revolution 2010, ethnic clashes (Osh 2010), constitutional shifts, and Manas epic heritage.

religion.note: Nomadic Kyrgyz Islam blended with Tengrism/shamanic traditions; growing conservative Islam; secular constitution

ethnic_groups.name: Kyrgyz
ethnic_groups.notes: Turkic; 40 tribes reflected on national flag (40-ray sun); nomadic pastoralist heritage; Manas epic (500,000+ lines); north-south clan divide; yurt culture

ethnic_groups.name: Uzbek
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern Kyrgyzstan (Osh, Jalal-Abad); settled/farming; 2010 ethnic violence killed ~470; tension over representation; distinct from northern-dominated politics

ethnic_groups.name: Russian
ethnic_groups.notes: Declining (was 21% in 1989); Bishkek/Chuy; Soviet settlers; educated professionals; many emigrated

ethnic_groups.name: Dungan (Chinese Hui Muslim)
ethnic_groups.notes: Fled China 1877-1878; Karakol area; speak Gansu Mandarin in Cyrillic; farming; unique cuisine

ethnic_groups.name: Uyghur
ethnic_groups.notes: Turkic; trade; Bishkek/Tokmok; Chinese border areas

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Tajik, Tatar, Ukrainian, Korean, German)
ethnic_groups.notes: Tajik minority in south; Soviet-era deportee communities; small but culturally distinct

country_profile.notes_unique: Only Central Asian country to have had two successful revolutions (2005, 2010); 'Switzerland of Central Asia' (mountainous, 94% above 1000m); Issyk-Kul (world's second-largest alpine lake); Epic of Manas (UNESCO intangible heritage); nomadic games (kok-boru/buzkashi)

current_leader.name: Sadyr Japarov
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Came to power after October 2020 protests; was imprisoned for hostage-taking; populist; pushed new constitution (2021) expanding presidential powers; nationalist; Kumtor gold mine nationalisation

former_presidents.name: Sooronbay Jeenbekov
former_presidents.notes: Resigned after post-election protests October 2020; southern Kyrgyz

former_presidents.name: Almazbek Atambayev
former_presidents.notes: First peaceful transfer; later arrested on corruption charges; stormed by security forces 2019; sentenced then freed then re-arrested

former_presidents.name: Roza Otunbayeva
former_presidents.notes: Transitional president after April Revolution; Central Asia's first female head of state; oversaw new parliamentary constitution

former_presidents.name: Kurmanbek Bakiyev
former_presidents.notes: Tulip Revolution brought to power; became authoritarian; family corruption; overthrown April 2010; fled to Belarus

former_presidents.name: Askar Akayev
former_presidents.notes: Physicist; initially democratic reformer ('island of democracy'); became authoritarian; overthrown in Tulip Revolution; fled to Russia

910.name: Ancient Tian Shan Cultures
910.description: The earliest known cultures of the Tian Shan mountain region, from Bronze Age petroglyphs to the Saka and Wusun nomadic confederations around Issyk-Kul and the Fergana Valley.

sub_clusters.name: Petroglyphs and Bronze Age Settlements
sub_clusters.description: The Saimaluu-Tash petroglyph site with over 10,000 rock engravings, Bronze Age settlements in the Fergana and Chuy valleys, and early pastoral nomadism in the Tian Shan.

sub_clusters.name: Saka and Wusun Confederations
sub_clusters.description: The Saka (Scythian) presence in the Tian Shan, their displacement by the Wusun people around Issyk-Kul, and Chinese Han dynasty diplomatic contact with the Wusun.
key_events: Zhang Qian's diplomatic mission contacts the Wusun around Issyk-Kul (c. 119 BC)

910.name: Turkic Khaganates and Kyrgyz Origins
910.description: The Göktürk and subsequent Turkic states in the Tian Shan region, the Yenisei Kyrgyz Great Power era, and the establishment of a distinct Kyrgyz ethnic and political identity.

sub_clusters.name: Göktürk and Uyghur Periods
sub_clusters.description: The Tian Shan region under successive Turkic khaganates, the Uyghur Khaganate's dominance, and the rise of the Yenisei Kyrgyz as a major steppe power.

sub_clusters.name: Yenisei Kyrgyz Great Power
sub_clusters.description: The Kyrgyz destruction of the Uyghur Khaganate in 840, establishing the 'Kyrgyz Great Power' era, the expansion across the steppe, and eventual withdrawal back to the Yenisei.
key_events: Yenisei Kyrgyz overthrow the Uyghur Khaganate — beginning of the Kyrgyz Great Power era (840 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Karakhanid Islamization
sub_clusters.description: The Karakhanid dynasty's rule over the Tian Shan region, the spread of Islam among Turkic peoples, Balasagun as a major cultural center, and the composition of the Kutadgu Bilig.
key_events: Yusuf Balasaguni composes the Kutadgu Bilig (Wisdom of Royal Glory) in Balasagun (1069–1070)

920.name: Mongol and Chagatai Period
920.description: The Mongol conquest of the Tian Shan region, its incorporation into the Chagatai Khanate, the Moghulistan state, and the migration of Kyrgyz tribes southward into the Tian Shan mountains.

sub_clusters.name: Mongol Conquest and Chagatai Khanate
sub_clusters.description: The Mongol conquest of the Karakhanid and Kara-Khitai states, the region's assignment to the Chagatai ulus, and the gradual Turkicization of the Mongol rulers.
key_events: Genghis Khan subjugates the Kyrgyz tribes of the Yenisei region (1207)

sub_clusters.name: Moghulistan and Kyrgyz Migration
sub_clusters.description: The Moghulistan state in the eastern Chagatai territories, the southward migration of Kyrgyz tribes from the Yenisei to the Tian Shan, and the formation of the distinct Kyrgyz ethnic identity.

920.name: Kyrgyz Tribal Confederation
920.description: The emergence of a distinct Kyrgyz tribal society in the Tian Shan, the oral epic Manas, conflicts with the Dzungar Mongols and the Kokand Khanate, and the formation of tribal wings (kanat).

sub_clusters.name: Epic of Manas and Tribal Identity
sub_clusters.description: The crystallization of Kyrgyz identity around the oral Epic of Manas — one of the world's longest epic poems — the tribal structure of left (sol) and right (ong) wings, and mountain nomadic culture.
key_events: The Epic of Manas — 500,000 lines, the longest oral epic in the world — transmitted through generations of manaschi bards

sub_clusters.name: Dzungar Conflicts and Kokand Subjugation
sub_clusters.description: Devastating Dzungar Mongol raids into Kyrgyz territory, the Qing destruction of the Dzungar state, and the subsequent expansion of the Kokand Khanate over the Kyrgyz tribes.

930.name: Kokand Khanate Rule
930.description: The Kokand Khanate's domination of the Kyrgyz tribes, the construction of fortresses in the Chuy and Fergana valleys, heavy taxation and resistance, and the Russian conquest of the khanate.

sub_clusters.name: Kokand Fortresses and Kyrgyz Resistance
sub_clusters.description: The Kokand Khanate's establishment of fortresses like Pishpek (Bishkek) and Tokmok to control the Kyrgyz, heavy tributary demands, and periodic Kyrgyz rebellions.
key_events: Kokand Khanate builds the fortress of Pishpek on the site of modern Bishkek (1825)

sub_clusters.name: Russian Conquest of Kokand
sub_clusters.description: Russian forces under Generals Cherniaev and von Kaufman conquer Kokand territories, some Kyrgyz leaders ally with Russia against Kokand, and the khanate is abolished and annexed.
key_events: Russia abolishes the Kokand Khanate and incorporates Kyrgyz lands into Turkestan (1876)

940.name: Russian Colonial Rule
940.description: The incorporation of Kyrgyz lands into Russian Turkestan, Slavic settler colonialism disrupting nomadic pastoralism, and the catastrophic 1916 Revolt and its brutal suppression.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Settlement and Land Seizure
sub_clusters.description: The influx of Russian and Ukrainian settlers seizing prime Kyrgyz pastures in the Chuy and Issyk-Kul valleys, forced sedentarization policies, and growing resentment.

sub_clusters.name: 1916 Ürkün Revolt
sub_clusters.description: The 1916 Central Asian Revolt against conscription, the catastrophic Russian reprisals, and the Ürkün (Exodus) — the mass flight of Kyrgyz to China resulting in the death of an estimated one-third of the Kyrgyz population.
key_events: Ürkün (Exodus) — mass flight to China after brutal suppression of the 1916 revolt, with enormous loss of life

950.name: Soviet Kyrgyzstan
950.description: Kyrgyzstan under Soviet rule: the Basmachi resistance, national delimitation creating the Kyrgyz SSR, collectivization, Russification, the development of a literary culture, and the perestroika-era ethnic clashes.

sub_clusters.name: Basmachi Resistance and National Delimitation
sub_clusters.description: The Basmachi movement's guerrilla resistance against Soviet rule, Stalin's national delimitation creating a Kyrgyz ASSR (1926) and then SSR (1936), and the early construction of Kyrgyz national identity.
key_events: Soviet national delimitation creates the Kara-Kyrgyz Autonomous Oblast (1924)
Kyrgyz SSR established as a full Soviet republic (1936)

sub_clusters.name: Soviet Modernization and Osh Conflict
sub_clusters.description: Soviet industrialization and literacy campaigns, the creation of Kyrgyz literary language, writer Chingiz Aitmatov's international fame, and the 1990 Osh ethnic clashes between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks.
key_events: Chingiz Aitmatov publishes 'The Day Lasts More Than a Hundred Years,' bringing Kyrgyz literature to world attention (1980)
Osh ethnic riots between Kyrgyz and Uzbeks over land disputes (1990)

960.name: Independent Kyrgyzstan
960.description: Kyrgyzstan's turbulent independence: the 'Island of Democracy' under Akayev, two revolutions (2005, 2010), the 2010 ethnic violence in Osh, and ongoing political instability amid democratic aspirations.

sub_clusters.name: Akayev Era and Tulip Revolution
sub_clusters.description: Askar Akayev's presidency as Central Asia's initial 'Island of Democracy,' the slide toward authoritarianism and corruption, and the Tulip Revolution overthrowing him.
key_events: Kyrgyzstan declares independence from the Soviet Union (August 31, 1991)
Tulip Revolution — mass protests overthrow President Akayev (March 2005)

sub_clusters.name: Revolutions, Ethnic Violence, and New Politics
sub_clusters.description: Bakiyev's overthrow in 2010, the devastating Osh ethnic violence, the adoption of a parliamentary system, and Sadyr Japarov's rise to power after the 2020 political crisis.
key_events: Second revolution overthrows President Bakiyev; ethnic violence in Osh kills hundreds (April–June 2010)
Sadyr Japarov comes to power after the annulment of parliamentary elections (2020)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
